print_transformations.text: CheckBefore startingDuring treatmentBetween visitsResponse / follow-upAfter a hold or stopBloods and organ safetyFull blood count, kidney and liver tests; medicine review and pregnancy-prevention programme assessment for women and men. If pregnancy is possible, a supervised pregnancy test is needed within seven days before starting.Full blood count, kidney and liver tests every four weeks. Review cramps, strength, taste, eating, weight, hair/skin changes and treatment tolerance. Pregnancy testing is monthly when applicable, even if periods stop.Contact the team for new symptoms; extra tests may be needed between scheduled checks.Safety bloods do not by themselves show whether cancer is responding.Agree continuing clinical/skin review, any response imaging and support for ongoing effects. The pregnancy-prevention, donation and breastfeeding restrictions continue after the last dose for their specified periods.Cancer, skin and daily functionRecord diagnosis, stage, current disease sites and the baseline assessment.Keep the source-specific skin and clinical reviews and the individually agreed response assessments.Record new lesions, lumps, wound changes, pain and effects on usual activities.Write the next examination or scan date and the responsible team; no universal scan or tumour-marker interval is assumed.Keep follow-up for the treated lesion and for other skin cancers. Examination and any imaging are tailored to the disease and treatment; locally advanced disease needs an individual plan. Continuing precautions after vismodegib are part of follow-up even when the cancer medicine has stopped.Medicines and continuing precautionsReview all medicines and the pregnancy/fertility plan.Review treatment taken or received, holds, adverse effects and supportive medicines.Keep the actual urgent contacts and do not restart a held medicine yourself.Bring the medicine list and treatment summary to other services.Vismodegib can cause severe harm to an unborn baby. Women who could become pregnant need the formal pregnancy-prevention programme, including two recommended contraceptive methods (one highly effective method plus a barrier method), unless the agreed alternative is continuous abstinence, during treatment and for 24 months after stopping. Pregnancy tests are supervised before treatment and monthly, even with absent periods. Men must use a condom, with spermicide if available, during sex with a female partner during treatment and for two months afterwards, including after a vasectomy. Report a suspected patient or partner pregnancy immediately. Do not breastfeed or donate blood during treatment or for 24 months afterwards; do not donate semen during treatment or for two months afterwards. Ask the team to explain and document the full programme; this summary does not replace its materials.
